title: Going down and surjective spectrum bound Krull dimension
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings. Assume that $\varphi$ has the going-down property: whenever $\mathfrak p_1\subseteq\mathfrak p_2$ are prime ideals of $R$ and $\mathfrak q_2$ is a prime ideal of $S$ with $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q_2)=\mathfrak p_2$, there is a prime ideal $\mathfrak q_1\subseteq\mathfrak q_2$ of $S$ with $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q_1)=\mathfrak p_1$. Assume also that $\operatorname{Spec}S\to\operatorname{Spec}R$, $\mathfrak q\mapsto\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$, is surjective. Then $\dim R\le\dim S$, where dimension is Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring].

proof.text: If $R=0$, then it has no prime ideals and $\dim R=-\infty$, so the conclusion is immediate. Otherwise, let $\mathfrak p_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\mathfrak p_n$ be any finite strictly increasing chain of prime ideals of $R$. By surjectivity of $\operatorname{Spec}S\to\operatorname{Spec}R$, choose a prime $\mathfrak q_n$ of $S$ with $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q_n)=\mathfrak p_n$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00OH (lemma-dimension-going-up), proof: choose a prime over the final member of a chain

proof.text: Apply going down successively to the inclusions $\mathfrak p_{n-1}\subsetneq\mathfrak p_n,\ldots,\mathfrak p_0\subsetneq\mathfrak p_1$. This produces primes $\mathfrak q_i\subseteq\mathfrak q_{i+1}$ with $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q_i)=\mathfrak p_i$. Each inclusion is strict, because equality would imply equal contractions while $\mathfrak p_i\subsetneq\mathfrak p_{i+1}$. Thus $S$ has a strictly increasing prime chain of length $n$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00OH (lemma-dimension-going-up), proof: repeated going down and strictness from distinct contractions

proof.text: Every finite prime-chain length occurring in $R$ therefore occurs in $S$. Taking suprema of the chain lengths and using the definition of Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] gives $\dim R\le\dim S$ (and the same inequality is automatic in the $R=0$ case).
